title: Trump signs Russia sanctions bill into law, allowing up to 100% tariffs on India
content: President Trump has officially enacted a new sanctions law aimed at Russia and Iran, empowering the U.S. to impose penalties on nations purchasing Russian energy supplies. Countries like India and China, significant buyers of Russian crude and gas, have raised concerns about the potential impact on India-US relations and energy security. Both Russia and China have also expressed their discontent towards these sanctions.

title: US reaches deal with Denmark for ‘permanent security control’ over Greenland
content: The United States and Denmark are in the final stages of discussions to enhance US military operations in Greenland. This strategic arrangement will not infringe on Greenland's autonomy, affirming its status as a Danish territory. The talks also involve strategies to curb Chinese activity in this vital Arctic locale. A potential agreement might include establishing a US missile defense system, with an official update expected shortly.

title: Pawan Sehrawat replaces Tajinderpal Singh Toor as India's Asian Games flag-bearer
content: Pawan Sehrawat has been chosen as the flag-bearer for India's opening ceremony at the Asian Games, stepping in for Tajinderpal Singh Toor, who faced delays with his official kit. Toor mentioned that his kit would arrive too late to participate in the event. Additionally, the athletics team is still waiting for their uniforms. Sehrawat will accompany Manu Bhaker in carrying the Indian flag.

title: Meet Dina McCormick, whom Zuckerberg asked to trade her Meta board seat for a job
content: Born in Cairo, Egypt and raised in Texas, Dina Powell McCormick gave up her Meta board seat last December after Mark Zuckerberg asked her to take an operating job instead. Nine months on, the Goldman Sachs veteran and former deputy national security adviser is president, vice chairman and co-leader of Meta Compute, handling the company's hardest legal, political and financial problems as its 2026 AI capex guidance climbs to as much as $145 billion.

title: Trump bans news outlets CNN, MS NOW, Politico from White House
content: President Donald Trump has enacted a swift exclusion of three major news outlets—CNN, MS NOW, and Politico—from White House premises. He branded their regular reports as 'FAKE NEWS,' marking a bold stance against media he perceives as adversarial. Trump warned that more outlets could follow if they continue to publish misleading narratives about his presidency.

title: 'Haar nahi maanunga': Sujeet Kalkal's Asian Games 2026 gold mission on the road to LA Olympics
content: Wrestler Sujeet Kalkal’s Olympic dream was shattered before he could even step on the mat at the Paris qualifiers. Stranded at Dubai airport for three days, he arrived in Kyrgyzstan after the weigh-in had ended. Now, the 23-year-old is looking at the Asian Games as a fresh start. Representing India in the competitive 65kg category, Sujeet is determined to win gold and keep his Olympic dream alive.

title: $1.75m historic home mirrors Swift and Kelce's $5.35m Ohio mansion
content: A historic mansion linked to Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio estate has hit the market for $1.75 million. The House of Seven Gables in Illinois spans 10,000 square feet with seven bedrooms and was designed by the same architect who created Kelce’s 21,000-square-foot Moyenage estate overlooking Lake Erie.

title: Rod Stewart's former LA estate flips from $6.25m to $86m after restoration
content: A legendary estate in Holmby Hills, previously owned by Rod Stewart, has fetched an impressive $86 million. The sprawling six-acre property was split into two parcels, with television producer David Zander acquiring the main mansion for $57 million. Meanwhile, Nick Kaiser purchased a smaller parcel complete with a historic cabin for $29 million. This notable sale underscores the ongoing allure of grand historic properties.

title: Google cofounder Larry Page’s wife’s company has donated over $120m in ocean projects
content: Lucinda Southworth, married to Google co-founder Larry Page, is a passionate advocate for ocean conservation through her organization, Oceankind. Since 2018, Oceankind has generously contributed over $120 million to improve marine ecosystems and support community health. With a focus on addressing pressing challenges like climate change and pollution, the organization champions innovative solutions and effective policies to protect our oceans worldwide.

title: Simone Biles’ $3m mansion: How did she build her Texas lakefront estate?
content: Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens’ Texas lakefront mansion is finally complete after years of planning, approvals and construction delays. The couple started designing the home in 2020 and finished it in November 2025. The reported $3 million property includes a private gym, pool, sports court, large kitchen, spa-style bathroom, laundry room and a dedicated space for their dogs.

title: Sophie Cunningham’s inspiring journey: How did she rise to WNBA stardom?
content: Sophie Elizabeth Cunningham’s inspirational story is a tapestry of athletic versatility, family support, financial hardship and perseverance. Cunningham’s journey from Columbia, Missouri, to the WNBA and the Indiana Fever has been filled with both success and personal trials. Her college record, her professional career, her injuries, her demanding schedule, and her relationship with her fans give a broader view of an athlete whose story is much more than basketball.

title: Mamata moves Supreme Court against EC decision to freeze TMC name, symbol

Her faction received a new name and symbol for the October 6 elections. The rival faction was allotted a different name and symbol by the ECI. The dispute over the original party identity remains unresolved by the commission.

title: UN report finds widespread sexual violence in Ukraine war, 89% of cases linked to Russia

The report highlights the ongoing nature of these abhorrent acts amid the conflict.

title: Dengue vaccine to hit market by first half of 2027
content:
Details of the vaccine’s price were not available.

NEW DELHI: India's first dengue vaccine is expected to be available in the private market in the first half of 2027. Takeda Pharma and Dr Reddy's Laboratories have entered into an agreement under which the latter will promote and distribute QDENGA, the Japanese firm's dengue vaccine, across India's private market for paediatric and adult vaccination. The collaboration follows QDENGA's marketing authorisation by India's Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation in July for individuals aged 4 to 60 years. "While inclusion in India's public immunisation programme remains a key ambition, private-market availability will provide a pathway for eligible individuals to access the vaccine,'' a statement said. Details of the vaccine's price were not available.

title: Extremely speedy action by probe agency can create doubt: SC

title: Presumption of guilt doesn't make prosecution case 'gospel truth': SC
content: a bench of justices gave this ruling while setting aside concurrent judgments of a court and HC convicting a man, whom a woman falsely accused of sexually assaulting her minor daughter in a slum in south Delhi in 2015 . the bench said both the trial court and the HC appeared to have been swayed by the presumption of guilt provision in Pocso Act and overlooked glaring discrepancies .

title: Surinder Koli, accused and acquitted in 2006 Nithari killings, found dead
